obsidian.$description: Obsidian — Primary text, structural borders, and outline contours that define all surface edges

paper.$description: Paper — Page canvas, inverted text on dark surfaces, and button labels on green fills

gridline.$description: Gridline — Subtle dividers and light borders on secondary surfaces

slate.$description: Slate — Secondary text and muted UI elements

smoke.$description: Smoke — Mid-tier borders and inactive form strokes

fog.$description: Fog — Hairline borders and tertiary dividers

ash.$description: Ash — Faint outlines and placeholder chrome

graphite.$description: Graphite — Deemphasized body text and metadata

stone.$description: Stone — Tertiary captions and disabled states

bone.$description: Bone — Card surfaces and elevated panel backgrounds — one shade off white

voltage-green.$description: Voltage Green — Primary action buttons, active states, and live UI feedback — saturated green on black-and-white canvas reads as switched-on electricity

ember-orange.$description: Ember Orange — Orange action color for filled buttons, selected navigation states, and focused conversion moments

highlighter-yellow.$description: Highlighter Yellow — Decorative borders, selection marks, and editorial accent strokes — never used as fill

melange.$description: Display and headline type. Set at extreme sizes (71–146px) with aggressive negative tracking (-0.05 to -0.058em). The medium weight is deliberate — heavy enough to anchor, not so heavy it shouts. Brings editorial magazine energy; no system sans substitutes this

favorit-mono.$description: Micro-labels, UI chrome, and metadata. Tiny uppercase tracking at -0.03 to -0.037em creates Swiss editorial caption feel. Line-heights stretch to 2.4 for dense vertical stacks. Always set small — this is a caption font, never a body font

arial.$description: Fallback system body text. Likely a detection artifact; real product body is handled by the headline and mono systems. Treat as last-resort stack
